requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the sources satisfy `requirements.references.outline_comments`.** I read the code and tests below and found no unmarked implementation and no unspecified behavior. I did not run the tests.

**Implementation**
- **Comment grammar nodes.** Each profile defines `is_comment`.
  - Rust: `src/outline/rust.rs` `is_comment` (`line_comment` and `block_comment`).
  - Markdown: `src/outline/markdown.rs` `is_comment`, which matches only `html_block` nodes that start with `<!--` and end with `-->`. An inline HTML comment is therefore paragraph text of its section.
  - CSS, Python, TOML, TypeScript, TSX and YAML: `kind_is_comment` and the CSS `is_comment`, wired through their `PROFILE` statics.
  - `Profile` in `profile.rs` carries `comment_binds_to_container` and `trailing_comments_outside`.
- **Runs.** `assign_comments` in `src/outline/mod.rs` sorts the comments and joins one into the previous run only when all of these hold:
  - both comments have the same `binds_to_container` setting;
  - neither comment follows other source on its first line (`trails_code`);
  - only whitespace lies between them;
  - the second starts on the line after the first ends, or on the same line.

  A comment that follows code, including another comment, starts its own run. A blank line or any source in between splits a run.
- **Trailing comments.** `trailing_owner` gives such a run to the innermost node whose pre-widening line range covers that line. Among siblings sharing the line it picks the last one that starts before the comment.
- **Other runs.** `run_owner` finds the smallest node by byte range containing the run. The run belongs to the next child of that node that starts after it, and to the container itself when there is no such child. At top level the container is the root.
- **Container binding.** `run_owner` returns the container for runs that bind to it. Rust's `is_inner_doc_comment` binds `//!` and `/*!`, so file-level inner docs belong to the root.
- **References in comments.** Consumers use the owner assigned here. `comment_fences` records each fence's run owner. `owner_at_line` is used by `reference_selector` (authoring inputs), `reference_set_digest` and `citation_items`.
- **Rust item coverage.** `src/rust_coverage.rs` uses `comment.owner` and the fence owner. It is marked as an implementation of `rust_item_coverage`, whose text defers to this requirement. I treated that as the other requirement carrying out its part. Likewise `src/authoring/tools.rs` `references` and `search` use the owner functions under the authoring requirements that cite this one.
- **Implementation marking.** The core outline functions, structs, profiles and consumers all carry `{impl}` markers.

**Tests**
- **Core ownership.** `src/outline/tests.rs` covers the main cases:
  - `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container`: next-node ownership, container ownership, trailing comments, root-level tails and inner docs;
  - `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next`;
  - `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod`;
  - `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root`;
  - `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node`;
  - `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` (`//!` and `/*!`).
- **Per-language and edge cases.**
  - `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown, each with a lead run, a trailing comment, a comment after the last child, and a tail where applicable.
  - `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` covers the Markdown block-versus-inline rule.
  - `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers the rule that a comment following another comment forms its own run.
  - `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` and `workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows` cover the YAML specifics, the latter against the repository's own workflow files.
- **Consumers.** Run splitting and owners for fences are tested in `src/fenced.rs`. Owner-based inputs are tested in `authoring/inputs.rs` and `authoring/tools.rs`. Digest stability and sensitivity are tested in `evidence.rs`.

The tests cover the boundaries (blank-line splits, container versus next node, root fallback) and both comment kinds that bind to their container.

containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that

{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and

:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
